The full run had 34 failures, 2594 passes, 24 skips and 1 xfail. The failures are in 7 test files:

| Test file | Failures |
|---|---|
| `tests/test_arguments.py` | 1 (`test_nargs_star`) |
| `tests/test_basic.py` | 1 (`test_basic_functionality`) |
| `tests/test_commands.py` | 1 (`test_other_command_invoke`) |
| `tests/test_context.py` | 1 (`test_ensure_context_objects`) |
| `tests/test_options.py` | 1 (`test_prefixes`) |
| `tests/test_parser.py` | 5 (`test_split_arg_string[...]`) |
| `tests/test_utils/test_echo_via_pager.py` | 24 (`test_echo_via_pager[...]`) |

The console output was truncated after the first 10 failures. I got the other 24 from the saved full log, using the 34 traceback headers. I did not re-run the suite.

`tests/test_chain.py::test_group_chaining` is an expected failure (xfail), so I left it out.

The first five files and `test_parser.py` are the ones with uncommitted changes in git status. Their failures look inverted: the assertions read `assert not not None` and `assert not [...] == [...]`. That may be a side effect of those edits. I haven't confirmed it, and I haven't changed any files.

The `test_echo_via_pager.py` failures are a different kind. The pager output comes back empty (`'' == 'testtest\n'`). That file has no local modifications, so those failures are more likely an environment issue, such as `less` in this WSL setup.
